gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured chamber temperature for any of these printers. CNC Kitchen's thermocouples read 50.3 °C and 54.1 °C inside the Bambu Lab P2S's passive chamber, with the bed at 100–110 °C. Clever Creations timed the Creality K1C's chamber at 30 minutes to rise from 25 °C to its 38 °C maximum.
standout_why: I compared three pages. firstlayerlab.com is cited in chat 1. 3dprintgearlab.com is cited in both chats. layerwalker.com is a top result that wasn't cited. All three give 'Passive' with no temperature for the P2S, P1S and K1C. For the Q2 they give only QIDI's claimed 65 °C. layerwalker gives an unattributed '35 to 45 °C' for passive enclosures in general. None of them reports a measured chamber temperature, noise level, power draw or print time for any candidate. I could not open popularmechanics.com (cited in chat 2) or theverge.com, so I could not check those two.
decides: The measurements back ChatGPT's split pick and make it more precise. The P2S's passive chamber was measured at about 50–54 °C, which is far warmer than the K1C's measured 38 °C maximum. That makes the P2S a fair choice for occasional ABS/ASA. It also weakens the K1C as a choice for ABS. The case for the QIDI Q2's 65 °C active heater rests only on QIDI's own claim, because I found no independent measurement of it. So the Q2 pick for engineering filaments stays plausible but is not measured.

findings.label: Measured chamber temperature, passive (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann)
findings.value: 50.3 °C and 54.1 °C on two in-chamber thermocouple channels; 'around 50 °C or more' with the bed at 100–110 °C
findings.source_title: The P2S Is the Upgrade No One Expected – But Everyone Wanted! (CNC Kitchen, 2025-10-14)
findings.note: Thermocouple readings come from a photo caption. The text ties 'around 50 °C or more' to a 100–110 °C bed. No heat-up time is given, and the caption doesn't state the bed setpoint.

findings.label: Measured bed temperature spread (CNC Kitchen, FLIR thermal camera)
findings.source_title: The P2S Is the Upgrade No One Expected – But Everyone Wanted! (CNC Kitchen, 2025-10-14)
findings.note: FLIR thermal image of the heated bed. The center-to-corner difference is 8.8 °C.

findings.label: Measured chamber heat-up and maximum, passive (Clever Creations)
findings.source_title: Creality K1C Review: Minor Upgrades With Little Innovation | Clever Creations
findings.note: Lid on, all fans off. The bed setpoint for this test isn't stated. The page has no publication date; image paths suggest about March 2024. In the same review the bed peaked at about 95 °C when set to 100 °C.

findings.label: Measured noise (AndroidPCTV, Kim)
findings.value: 56 dB in normal use; 65 dB with the QIDI Box attached
findings.source_title: QIDI Q2 QIDI BOX, Review: CoreXY AMS 3D Printer (AndroidPCTV)
findings.note: No distance or method stated. The byline shows both 2025-08-20 and 2025-08-28. Same review: PLA Benchy printed in 20 minutes, ABS Buddha in 18 minutes.

findings.label: Measured noise and Benchy time (3Dwork, JJR)
findings.value: 50–60 dB during normal printing; Benchy in about 18 minutes
findings.source_title: QIDI Q2 Series + QIDI Box: Review (3Dwork, 2026-04-07)
findings.note: No distance, meter or method stated. 3Dwork names the fans and the Box feed mechanism as the main noise sources. QIDI Box color changes took 2–3 minutes each. The 65 °C chamber figure in this review is the maker's spec, not a measurement.

unsourced: A measured QIDI Q2 chamber temperature or heat-up time from a named reviewer. The Tom's Hardware and TechRadar Q2 reviews returned only their titles. The Printables 'Chamber Heat Insulation for Qidi Q2' post, which reportedly says a stock Q2 chamber takes at least an hour to reach 65 °C, returned 403. The '8–10 minutes to 65 °C' figure appears only on qiditech3dprinter.com, a QIDI-branded blog, with no stated method.
A measured chamber temperature for the Bambu Lab P1S from a named reviewer. I found only forum posts and unattributed guides.
Any named measurement for the Flashforge Adventurer 5M Pro (noise, chamber temperature, power).

A measured noise figure for the P2S or K1C with a stated distance from a named lab. Tom's Hardware's P2S review page returned only its title, and Notebookcheck has only a P2S launch article, not a review.
Measured power draw at the wall for any candidate. QIDI's 350 W + 280 W figure for the Q2 is a rating, not a measurement.
